Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AgenticTurnRetry

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AgenticTurnRetry
public final class AgenticTurnRetry extends Object
How a failed turn is retried (CIB7-2149).

The engine reads a retry cycle only for timer and async-continuation jobs, so a failed step was retried at once, three times within a fraction of a second, and then ended in an incident. The model call itself is already retried by LangChain4j; what that does not cover is a rate limit that lasts longer, or a step that fails elsewhere. A pause between the attempts gives those a chance.

The cycle is the scope's camunda:failedJobRetryTimeCycle, else the engine's failedJobRetryTimeCycle, else DEFAULT_RETRY_TIME_CYCLE. It is kept under a key of its own: the engine's key on the same activity belongs to the scope's own asynchronous continuation, and a default set there would change that job's retries too.

  • Method Details

    • configure

      public static void configure(Element scopeElement, ActivityImpl activity, AgenticToolCatalogParser.Parsing parsing)
      Parses the scope's retry cycle onto its activity. On a parse again a cycle of the scope that cannot be read is left out, and the next one in the order retries the turns: the engine's, else the default (CIB7-2367).

      Only the scope's own cycle is the model's, so only it refuses a deployment. The engine's is its configuration: one that cannot be read as text is logged, and the default retries the turns. The engine itself treats such a text cycle as unset for its own jobs. An engine cycle that is an expression which cannot be read is another matter: the engine refuses every model with an asynchronous element then, with an agent or without, as it always did.

    • read

      protected static FailedJobRetryConfiguration read(String cycle)
      The cycle read, or null when it cannot be. An expression that cannot be read throws an EL error, not a refusal, which on a parse again would block the definition (CIB7-2367). Unlike the agent's task, a cycle the node cannot read only gives way to the next one; the agent stays.

    • whyNot

      protected static String whyNot(String cycle)

    • because

    • cyclesOf

      protected static List<String> cyclesOf(Element scopeElement)
      The cycles that are set, in the order they apply: the scope's own, the engine's, and the default, which always ends the list. Without an engine in context, as outside a command, there is no engine's cycle.
